name: AI Deep Dive — ASML — 2026-05-02
rationale: ASML holds a structural monopoly on EUV lithography — the sole supplier of machines required to manufacture chips below 7nm. With 29% net margins, $11B TTM FCF, and High-NA EUV at $380M/machine beginning to ramp, fundamentals are exceptional. However at 47x trailing P/E ($1,427/share), the market is pricing in flawless execution of a multi-year growth runway. Our weighted DCF yields $1,353 (-5.2%), making ASML a marginal SELL on pure DCF — but the bull case ($2,629) reflects genuine platform optionality that a single-point estimate obscures.

bear.rationale: China export restrictions tighten further (all immersion DUV blocked) and global fab capex enters a correction cycle as memory/logic customers delay discretionary expansions. Revenue grows only 10% CAGR via pricing and limited volume. Margin compresses to 26% (still well above equipment industry average — ASML's monopoly floor) as High-NA ramp costs dilute near-term. Exit PE 22x reflects multiple compression from demand uncertainty. QM 0.95 — moats intact but macro headwinds prevent premium. Year 5 revenue $52.6B, EPS $35.49, price $741.76, PV $460.58.

base.rationale: Through-cycle execution. Analyst consensus ~19-21% Y1/Y2; 5-yr CAGR derived at 17% via natural deceleration (Y3→17%, Y4→14%, Y5→12%). Net margin 29% = TTM anchor; stable within historical 26-30% band (4yr avg 27.8%). Exit PE 30x appropriate for secular growth monopoly with service recurring revenue. QM 1.10: Moat 1 — sole EUV supplier (zero substitutes for sub-7nm chipmaking); Moat 2 — 5,500+ installed systems generating recurring service/upgrade revenue (~25% of total). Moderate buybacks offset dilution. Year 5 revenue $71.6B, EPS $56.67, price $1,870, PV $1,161.14.

bull.rationale: Catalyst: High-NA EUV ($380M+/machine) becomes the dominant platform for <2nm manufacturing. TSMC orders 10+, Samsung 8+, Intel 5+ High-NA units by 2027 — each unit ~2x revenue of standard EUV. China partial regulatory relief restores $2-3B of previously blocked revenue. Revenue grows 25% CAGR. Net margin expands to 33% as High-NA machines carry premium gross margins. Exit PE 40x = semiconductor growth ceiling (benchmark). QM 1.15 CITED: ASML demonstrates 'exceptional durable pricing power across cycles' — EUV machines priced from $100M (2012) → $200M (2020) → $380M (2025), increasing 3.8x over 13 years with no customer defection possible. This is the only company in InvestmentToolkit's coverage universe where QM > 1.1 is formally justified. Year 5 revenue $99.7B, EPS $92.06, price $4,234.70, PV $2,629.41.

aiThesis.rationale:
ASML is a technology monopoly — the only company manufacturing EUV lithography systems required for all leading-edge chip production below 7nm. This is not a durable competitive advantage; it is structural dependency. TSMC, Samsung, and Intel cannot build their next-generation fabs without ASML machines, and there is no alternative supplier on any realistic horizon. Pricing power is demonstrated and cross-cycle: EUV machine prices have risen from $100M (2012) to $200M (2020) to $380M+ (2025 High-NA) — a 3.8x increase over 13 years with no customer ability to defect. Margins have been remarkably stable at 26-30% through multiple industry cycles.

The central valuation tension is between exceptional quality and demanding price. At $1,427/share (47x trailing P/E), the market is pricing in a sustained high-growth trajectory that is achievable but requires everything to go right. Our base case (50% weight) — 17% CAGR, 29% margins, 30x exit PE — gives $1,161/share (-18.6% from current). The weighted fair value of $1,353 is only 5.2% below current price, making this a marginal rather than convicted SELL.

The China export restriction risk is real and underappreciated. China represented approximately $3B of FY2024 revenue and all advanced DUV immersion + EUV is now blocked. Further tightening or enforcement complications could remove another $1-2B annually. Conversely, any regulatory relief would be a significant positive catalyst.

High-NA EUV represents the most significant bull catalyst: at $380M+/machine versus $200M standard EUV, a successful High-NA ramp would dramatically accelerate revenue growth and margin expansion simultaneously. However, High-NA adoption depends on chipmakers committing capital to a technology that has limited volume production history — this is a real ramp risk.

The analyst community is decidedly bullish: 15 analysts, target mean $1,661 (+16%), strong buy consensus. Our DCF, using conservative 17% base CAGR and 30x exit PE, gives a lower number than analysts due to more conservative multiple assumptions. The spread between our bear ($460) and bull ($2,629) illustrates the binary optionality embedded in this monopoly.

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: Used API shares_diluted 385.4M. Cross-check: mktcap $550.0B / price $1,427.02 = 385.4M — perfect 0% discrepancy. NI/EPS check: $9,609.4M / $24.73 = 388.6M (0.8% rounding — within normal). Note: ASML reports in EUR; API values appear USD-converted. EPS figures may reflect EUR/USD translation factor — flagged as data quality note but not material for DCF.
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM 29.42% used. Historical: 26.56% → 28.44% → 26.79% → 29.42% (4yr avg 27.80%). Narrow 4pp band — stable-trending upward. TTM used per Step 3 Rule 9 (consistent 3-yr improvement trend with only minor FY3 dip). Base margin 29% = TTM anchor. Bear 26% = below TTM reflecting China/cycle headwinds. Bull 33% = High-NA mix uplift (high-margin capital equipment).
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Y1 analyst rev $38.93B (+19.2%), Y2 $47.01B (+20.8%). Neither exceeds 40% — no hypergrowth exception. Deceleration path: Y3→17%, Y4→14%, Y5→12%. Y5 base revenue = $71.6B from $32.67B TTM → 5yr CAGR = (71.6/32.67)^0.2-1 = 17.0%. Blended consensus ~20%. Base 17% = within ±3pp of blended 20% per Rule 7. Bear 10% = China restriction downside. Bull 25% = High-NA ramp uplift.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Technology — Semiconductor Equipment & Materials. Using Semiconductor Equipment benchmark: conservative P/E 20, median P/E 28-30, growth P/E 40-45. ASML monopoly position justifies median-to-growth P/E range. Bear 22x (below benchmark median — demand uncertainty premium). Base 30x (benchmark median-top end). Bull 40x (benchmark growth ceiling).
dataQualityFlags: EUR/USD translation: ASML reports in EUR; API price in USD. EPS figures appear USD-converted. PE ratios API-computed (47.2x trailing vs implied $1,427/$24.73 = 57.7x) suggest possible EUR EPS in API fields. Flag: PE metrics may have currency inconsistency. Does not affect DCF (NI-based).

Financials historical Year 1 all zeros: revenue, NI, FCF, margins show 0 for oldest year. 4-yr array effectively 3 real years + 1 zero. Excluded zero year from margin averaging (4yr avg computed on 3 valid years + TTM).

FCF lumpiness: $7.17B → $3.25B → $9.08B → $11.03B. Likely capex timing (major facility investment in FY2). TTM FCF $11.03B is exceptional — not used as primary DCF input but noted as strong quality signal.

Forward PE discrepancy: API forward_pe 29.8x implies NTM EPS ~$47.8, but CY2026 analyst consensus $31.34. Gap likely reflects NTM vs calendar year alignment and EUR/USD translation. Used revenue-based DCF rather than EPS-based to avoid this ambiguity.

priorAnalysisReview.assumptionAudit: Prior base QM 1.25 and bull QM 1.30 both exceed 1.10 threshold with no moat citations in rationale. Bear weight only 0.20 — underweights material China export restriction risk (China was ~$3B revenue in FY2024). Bear growth 10%/margin 25% reasonable but PE 20 slightly low for bear case. Prior reached similar SELL conclusion ($1,220.98) but via unvalidated QM inflation rather than grounded benchmark analysis. This analysis corrects: (a) QM 1.10 base / 1.15 bull with explicit moat citations; (b) bear weight raised to 25%; (c) growth anchored to analyst deceleration path rather than round-number selection.

priorAnalysisReview.fundamentalChanges: High-NA EUV deliveries underway (TSMC, Intel). China DUV immersion restrictions tightened. Analyst consensus raised for FY2026-2027. Piotroski score 8/9 — strong financial health.

analyticsLog.confidenceBreakdown: 0.82/1.0 — Base 1.0. +0.08 monopoly moat (no substitutes for EUV); +0.05 Piotroski 8/9 financial health; +0.03 strong analyst coverage (15 analysts, tight range); -0.05 EUR/USD translation uncertainty in API metrics; -0.05 China restriction swing risk (binary outcome); -0.08 High-NA adoption pace uncertainty (largest individual uncertainty); -0.06 lumpy FCF creates visibility issues; +0.02 High-NA moat strengthens across cycle (cross-cycle pricing power confirmed)
